title: First-Run Setup Wizard
subtitle: Complete the minimum runtime configuration before handing the platform to end users.
milestone_desc: This wizard focuses on file-based bootstrap settings: security, storage, data source, AI, trading, branding, and review.

deployment.public: Public deployment with stricter auth expectations

hints.encryption_key: Changing this later can make previously encrypted credentials unreadable.
hints.enable_login: When disabled, the app stays accessible without authentication.
hints.enable_ai: AI is optional. Leaving it disabled keeps analysis features unavailable.
hints.enable_trading: Prefer paper mode first. Live mode requires explicit acknowledgement and full credentials.

validation.logto: All Logto fields are required when login is enabled.
validation.eodhd: EODHD API key is required when EODHD is enabled.
validation.openai: OpenAI API key is required when AI is enabled.
validation.trading_credentials: Trading credentials are required for the selected exchange and mode.
validation.live_ack: Live mode requires explicit risk acknowledgement.
validation.ai_provider: Enable at least one AI provider.
validation.ai_provider_keys: API key is required for all enabled AI providers.
validation.paper_credentials: Binance paper credentials require both API key and secret.
validation.live_credentials: Binance live credentials require both API key and secret.
validation.live_mode: Enable live trading before selecting live as the default mode.
validation.live_credentials_required: Live trading requires Binance live credentials.

guide.paper_intro: Use Binance Spot Test Network to generate sandbox credentials for paper mode, then keep the sandbox URL and credentials in the paper configuration below.
guide.paper_step_1: Open Binance Spot Test Network and sign in with a supported account to access the sandbox environment.
guide.paper_step_2: Generate a sandbox API key and secret from the testnet page, then copy both values immediately.
guide.paper_step_3: Keep the sandbox URL set to https://testnet.binance.vision and use these credentials only for paper mode.
guide.paper_step_4: Do not reuse live exchange keys here. Paper mode should stay isolated from your real trading account.
guide.paper_step_5: Paste the sandbox key pair into the paper tab below and run the paper test against testnet.
guide.paper_warning: Sandbox credentials are for paper mode only. Keep live credentials out of the paper tab, and leave the sandbox URL pointed at Binance Spot Test Network.
guide.live_intro: Create the key from Binance API Management, enable only the permissions you actually need, then lock it down with IP restrictions before pasting it back here.
guide.live_step_1: Open Binance API Management and click Create API, then choose a system-generated key.
guide.live_step_2: Complete Binance security verification and copy the API Key and Secret Key immediately.
guide.live_step_3: Enable only the permissions you need. For this app, keep Enable Reading on; enable Spot & Margin Trading only if you plan to place live orders.
guide.live_step_4: In API restrictions, set Restrict access to trusted IPs only and add the server public IP that will run this platform.
guide.live_step_5: Use separate keys for separate environments when possible, then paste the key pair here and run the live test button.
guide.live_warning: Binance recommends enabling only required permissions, storing secrets outside source control, rotating keys regularly, and deleting or replacing a key immediately if it may have been exposed.

ai_note: The wizard stores provider credentials and fallback priority. Runtime model names can be configured later in Settings.
trading_note: The onboarding flow only supports Binance and lets you configure paper and live credentials together.
